cohort: 350 antenatal women with singleton pregnancies and without any pre-existing medical disorders were screened.
finding: The study found a prevalence of hypothyroidism at 11.14%, with lower segment caesarean section being the most common mode of delivery among hypothyroid women, and identified various associated adverse feto-maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) was the most common mode of delivery in women with hypothyroidism.
followup_time: up to the point of delivery
